biography: Alessandro Pier Guidi's journey began not on a racetrack, but amidst the sun-drenched olive groves of Tuscany. Born into a family of modest means, his racing ambitions were fueled by a tattered copy of 'Grand Prix' magazine and a go-kart cobbled together from spare parts. He spent countless hours honing his skills on makeshift circuits around the family farm, his natural talent undeniable. A local karting championship win caught the eye of Milano GT36, who offered him a spot in their young driver program. The pressure was immense, but Alessandro's cool demeanor and strategic mind allowed him to excel. His climb through the ranks was meteoric, marked by calculated risks and a relentless pursuit of perfection. Now at what seems to be the peak of his career, Alessandro is considered a force to be reckoned with, his name whispered with respect and a hint of trepidation in the paddocks.
drivingStyle: Alessandro's driving style is best described as 'clinical'. He isn't one for flamboyant displays of aggression; instead, he meticulously analyzes every corner, every braking point, every nuance of the track. Tire management is his forte, often nursing his rubber to the finish while others falter. He possesses an uncanny ability to absorb pressure, remaining calm and collected even in the most chaotic of racing situations. His approach is calculating, prioritizing consistency and minimizing errors, a strategic chess master behind the wheel.

careerHighlight: Winning the GT Italia Championship in 2022 after a nail-biting final race where he overtook the leader on the last corner.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the 24 Hours of Monza in 2021 due to a mechanical failure while leading the race, costing his team a potential victory.
